claims.text: As-cast HfNbTaTiZr is a homogeneous single-phase BCC alloy.
Cold rolling and aging increase defect densities in HfNbTaTiZr and favor local ordering.
Cold rolling introduces dislocation networks into HfNbTaTiZr.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at 600–800 °C produces microstructural evolution relevant to its mechanical and thermoelastic response.
Local lattice distortions form through transient nanoscale ordering or early-stage precipitation and locally modify lattice parameters.
Thermal and mechanical loading induce processing-dependent microstructural reconfigurations such as ordering or precipitation.
Processing-induced local distortions disrupt homogeneous lattice expansion.
Local lattice distortions and thermal-expansion mismatch create heterogeneous internal stress fields.
The heterogeneous stress fields modify dislocation mobility.
Local distortions modify the alloy's effective elastic constants.
A common internal-stress mechanism couples high-temperature creep, elastic-modulus variation, microhardness, and thermal expansion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Cold-rolled and aged specimens in which local distortions are detected will show deviations from homogeneous-lattice creep predictions, including nonlinearities around 1250 °C.
Specimens containing local distortions will exhibit anomalous elastic-modulus trends between 293 K and 1100 K.
Cold-rolled and aged specimens containing local distortions will exhibit altered thermal-expansion behavior.
As-cast specimens lack the proposed local distortions and should follow homogeneous-lattice predictions.
A homogeneous BCC lattice without local ordering predicts linear thermal expansion, standard elastic-modulus trends, and conventional tensile-creep behavior.
At lower temperatures or low deformation levels, the alloy should behave more like the homogeneous-lattice baseline.
Using identical loading and heating protocols for as-cast, cold-rolled, and aged specimens provides a controlled comparison of processing-induced effects.
